publications.title: De Suspensione: Inflection, Composition, and the Long Drift Outward
publications.highlight: On suspensio, the inner act of holding thought while form catches up. Latin inflection, digital memory, and generative AI.
publications.abstract: Three historical migrations — the Latin-to-Romance simplification, the digital externalization of memory, and the offloading of sentence production to generative AI — converge on a single mental practice: suspensio, the inner act of composition once trained by the Trivium and by case-marking grammars that obliged the speaker to track relation internally. Drawing on classical-language impact studies, Romance morphosyntactic typology, neuro- and psycholinguistic work on grammar and thought, and recent empirical work on cognitive offloading and large language models, the paper rejects the strong Whorfian thesis that simplification produced cultural shallowness, defending instead the narrower claim that form, content, and production now migrate outward together — and that compositional practice can thin under AI assistance.

publications.title: Uncovering Candidate Potential with Multi-Modal AI Assessments
authors: Rumi Alexander Elías Calles et al.
publications.highlight: AI Match Score beats résumé screening by 16% AUC and finds 2× more qualified candidates.
publications.abstract: Our AI Match Score combines resume analysis, structured interviews, and role-specific evaluations to outperform traditional screening by 16% (AUC: 0.742 vs. 0.641). It surfaces nearly twice as many qualified candidates, capturing unique potential signals beyond what resumes reveal.

publications.title: From Plato to Pixels: Imagination, AI, and the Whole
authors: Rumi Alexander Elías Calles et al.
publications.highlight: Imagination from Plato's Forms to generative AI. What machines still cannot make.
publications.abstract: This philosophical exploration traces imagination's evolution from Plato's Forms through medieval theology to modern fragmentation, examining whether AI can truly simulate human creativity. It argues that imagination remains humanity's essential faculty for synthesizing meaning from chaos, even as machines attempt to replicate creation.

publications.title: Evaluating Speech-to-Text x LLM x Text-to-Speech Combinations for AI Interview Systems
authors: Rumi Alexander Elías Calles et al.
publications.abstract: We present a large-scale empirical comparison of speech-to-text, LLM, and text-to-speech combinations using data from over 300,000 AI-conducted job interviews. Our analysis reveals that Google's STT with GPT-4.1 and Cartesia's TTS outperforms alternatives in both objective quality metrics and user satisfaction scores.
